schemaNote: Procedural (synthesised) combat/UI SFX. Generated by ./GENERATE.sh with ffmpeg lavfi sources only — no sampled material, no third-party audio, so no CREDITS.md entry is needed (own work, effectively CC0). Format: 16-bit PCM mono 44.1 kHz WAV. WAV rather than MP3 on purpose: MP3 encoder delay/padding is applied inconsistently by browser decodeAudioData and would smear a 40 ms transient; these clips are tiny so raw PCM is free. Every clip is peak-normalised to -3.0 dBFS — relative loudness between events is set by `gain` in content/config/audio-map.json, never by re-rendering the file. `meanDb` below is the measured mean (RMS) level and is what the per-event gain was chosen against: a dense tonal clip (low negative meanDb) needs a much smaller gain than a sparse transient.
reason: The 21 imported w3x clips in ../ are all Chinese voice quips (kill/death/announce lines). None of them is a swing, thud, tick, projectile or cast sound, so the high-frequency combat events had no legible mapping. These fill exactly that gap.

clips.recipe: pink noise, 2x highpass 650 Hz + lowpass 6 kHz, 45 ms qsin swell then 155 ms exponential decay — an air whoosh, no pitch.
brown noise, lowpass 1.1 kHz, 4 ms attack + exponential decay — a soft low 'tk' tell, deliberately duller and quieter than swing.wav so the pair reads as tell -> swing.
sine sweep 150 -> 60 Hz (exp decay) mixed with a 50 ms pink-noise snap (900 Hz - 4.5 kHz) — body + transient; the meatiest clip in the set because the hit is the moment that must land.

white noise, 1.6 - 5.2 kHz, 2 ms attack + exponential decay — a hair-thin confirm tick. Fires on EVERY damage packet (DoTs, AoE, multi-hit), so it is the smallest clip in the set and carries the lowest gain.
descending sine chirp 1200 -> 300 Hz over 120 ms + a 30 ms high-noise transient — a dry 'pew'.
pink-noise burst 350 Hz - 4.8 kHz over a 260 Hz sine body, both exponentially decayed — a splat, distinctly brighter and shorter than thud.wav so projectile hits never read as auto-attack hits.
rising chirp 300 -> 900 Hz plus its octave, 50 ms qsin in / 120 ms qsin out — reads as 'winding up'. Densest clip in the set (sustained tone), hence the smallest gain.
A5 + E6 sine ping, 4 ms attack + exponential decay — the resolved counterpart to cast_begin's rise.
descending sine sweep 700 -> 150 Hz + a lowpassed brown-noise thump — falls where cast_begin rises, so an interrupt is audibly the opposite of a cast.
E5 + B5 sine chime, 30 ms swell + long exponential decay — an ambient 'something appeared', quiet enough to ignore mid-fight.
A5 + E6 + A6 sine bloom with a 250 ms high-noise sparkle — the reward payoff; same chime family as flowerSpawn but brighter, longer and a fifth higher.
descending 900 Hz sine chirp + 1.8-7 kHz band-passed white noise, both exp-decayed — an arcane 'fzzt', distinct from the physical thud so a magic hit reads differently by ear.
D6 + high-fifth sine ping, 2 ms attack + exp decay — a clean, pure bell for un-mitigated true damage.
1.2-6 kHz white-noise clank over a 520+780 Hz mid ring — a short metallic guard, the lighter '擋下' counterpart to guard_break.

clips.event: guardBreak (破防 — shield broke this frame)
clips.recipe: descending 1100 Hz sine sweep + bright 2.5 kHz+ noise burst — a glassy shatter, the bigger reaction when the shield breaks.
fast rising 700 Hz up-chirp + a 3 kHz+ transient — a sharp bright 'shing' for critical strikes.
double-highpassed 900 Hz pink whoosh, airier and higher than swing.wav — the over-commit of a missed melee.
descending 110 Hz sine body-thump + low-passed brown-noise debris — a heavy 'whump' as the victim hits the ground.
70 ms brown-noise blip low-passed at 900 Hz — a soft, very quiet step; fired only for the local player, cooldown-gated.

A5 880 Hz sine + 1760 Hz octave bite with a 20 ms 2.5 kHz+ noise click, 3 ms attack + exponential decay — a narrow-band beep that reads over the champSelect music bed. Tonal on purpose: a noise transient (tick.wav) disappears under BGM.

E6 1320 Hz with a slight upward bend + 1980/2640 Hz partials and a 50 ms 3 kHz+ noise attack, 360 ms exponential tail — an octave-higher, ~3x longer 'GO' that can never be mistaken for count-tick.wav.

Low craft flyby (task #86). Replaces the REJECTED rising-chirp (two chirps 1400->3100 Hz & 2100->4650 Hz, spectral flatness 0.000) that read as 泡泡龍 because rising+bright+tonal = "floating up". A Mach-0.56 source passes the listener at ~6 m: the retarded-time equation (a quadratic in emission time, solved in-line in aevalsrc) drives EXACT doppler pitch, 1/R loudness, per-band air absorption and an L->R pan at once. A 6-band noise filterbank whose bands decay top-first (tau~(150/f)^Q) FORCES the centroid down (1328->309 Hz over the first 120 ms, buoyancy 0.00 oct vs the chirp’s +0.21); each band carries a fast+slow time constant so air survives the head without re-brightening. A DRIFT term keeps concurrent copies off a shared fundamental (3x sub-300 pile-up +4.0 dB, near the incoherent +4.77). Kept the Akira ring-out the user liked (975 ms to -60 dB, low-passed before wide per-channel echo taps). AIR (12% at 2-8 kHz, SFM 0.48) is what separates it from 低音放屁聲. Judged only by GATE-hover-cyber.py (ACCEPT 19/19); peak-normalised to -3.0 dBFS with astats (float peak +3.2 dBFS, so volumedetect would clip). Keep the centroid FALLING and buoyancy near 0 on any re-cut — that number is the bubble-vs-flyby distinction.
clips.channels: stereo (the ONE non-mono fx clip — the L->R traversal IS the effect; played with no pan so the baked image survives)

clips.recipe: The 3-choose-1 card LOCK-IN (task #110): a 厲害的科技音效, a heavy tech mechanism seating. Three layers strike together at t=0 — a brown-noise CONTACT chunk (150-1300 Hz, loudest so the onset is a machined strike), a WEIGHT body (sub sine 140->55 Hz + octave-down 70->28 Hz power), and a descending detuned resonator LOCK (520->300, 660->380 Hz + a fast metallic 1560 Hz partial; descending = terminal/confirm). One 55 ms echo tap + dark master (hp 42, lp 5000). Measured against the cues it must never be mistaken for: HARD 6.0 ms onset vs the #86 cyber-hover SWELL of ~30 ms; LOW 405 Hz spectral centroid vs the hover's 1948 Hz and count-final's 2678 Hz; 0.605 s — decisive, about half count-tick (1.20 s) / count-final (1.05 s) / hover (1.55 s). The #86 hover is now ALSO low-band (~0.96 under 500 Hz vs this clip's 0.85): that shared low world is deliberate — the confirm sits in it rather than fighting it, and is separated from the hover instead by the hard onset, the darker centroid and the short length (NOT by weight). Those axes ARE the 'weighty mechanical, not bright/bubbly' brief — see GATE-draft-confirm.py, which rejects the real hover and both bells; keep the centroid low and the onset hard on any re-cut.

combatJuiceNote: The nine clips from hit_magic.wav onward were added for task #3 (combat juice): distinct 物理/魔法/防禦/破防 + crit/whiff/knockdown/footstep voices for the per-frame combat-feedback layer. The type-differentiated HIT voice (物理 reuses thud.wav; 魔法/true have their own clips) is driven by the enriched `damage` event; block/guardBreak map the sim's shield/damage-reduction path. Same deterministic ffmpeg-lavfi synthesis as the originals — own work, effectively CC0, no third-party audio.
countdownNote: count-tick.wav / count-final.wav were added for task #30 (champ-select last-5-seconds countdown). They are the only clips in the set authored to be heard OVER a music bed (champSelect BGM), which is why both are narrow-band tonal rather than noise-transient. Both are peak-normalised to -3.0 dBFS exactly like the rest: the REQUIRED rising loudness across 5→2 s is the per-call `volume` option on playSfx (0.45/0.60/0.75/0.90, then 1.0 for the final second), never a differently-rendered file — see apps/client/src/audio/countdownCue.ts.
